Paper Title: Automated Machine Learning for Predicting Diabetic Retinopathy From Ultra-Widefield Retinal Images
Prediction Target: ≥1 step DR progression on clinical ETDRS scale (binary classification)
Training Dataset: Beetham Eye Institute, Joslin Diabetes Center, Boston (single center)
Secondary Metrics: Validation: Mild NPDR - Sens 0.72, Spec 0.63, Acc 64.3%; Moderate NPDR - Sens 0.80, Spec 0.72, Acc 73.8%; 2-step progression detected: 75% mild, 85% moderate; 1-year rapid progressors: 100% mild, 85% moderate
Potential Application: Rapid progressor identification; patient enrichment; DRSS trajectory prediction; personalized screening intervals
Key Findings/Notes: First autoML model using UWF imaging for DR progression. UWF captures peripheral lesions important for risk. Saliency maps highlight optic disc and peripapillary vessels - regions not typically evaluated in early NPDR. Perforamnce comparable to bespoke AI models. 100% sensitivity for mild NPDR progressing within 1 year. Personalized intervals could reduce costs >20% and appointments ~40%.
Limitations: Single-center dataset; small sample size (1,179 images); no true external validation; no visual acuity outcomes; limited to mild/moderate

Paper Title: Deep learning algorithm predicts diabetic retinopathy progression in individual patients
Model Architecture: Inception-v3 DCNNs (7 field-specific 'pillars') + Random Forest aggregation; transfer learning from ImageNet→Kaggle DR
Training Dataset: RIDE/RISE Phase 3 trials (sham-treated study eyes + untreated fellow eyes)
Secondary Metrics: Month 12: Sens 91%, Spec 65%; Month 24: Sens 79%, Spec 72%; Month 6: Sens 66%, Spec 77%; Central fields only (F1+F2): AUC 0.64 vs 0.79 with all 7 fields
Potential Application: Patient enrichment for clinical trials; DRSS trajectory prediction; rapid progressor identification; validates peripheral retina importance
Key Findings/Notes: First to predict individual patient DR progression using single-visit CFPs. Key finding: peripheral fields (F3-F7) more predictive than central (F1-F2); using only F1+F2 drops AUC from 0.79→0.64. Attribution maps highlight microaneurysms, hemorrhages, exudates. SHAP shows F5 and F7 most important. Baseline DRSS grade alone achieves only AUC ~0.52. Explicitly designed for clinical trial enrichment.
Limitations: Small dataset (~530 patients); clinical trial population only (RIDE/RISE eligibility); no external validation; 7-field CFPs impractical vs single-field/UWF; only untreated eyes - no treatment effect modeling; limited interpretability; Roche/Genentech sponsored

A deep learning system for detecting diabetic retinopathy across the disease spectrum
Prediction Target: DR grade (5 levels: non-DR to PDR); DME; Lesion detection (microaneurysms, CWS, hard exudates, hemorrhages)
Model Architecture: DeepDR: Transfer learning multi-task network with 3 sub-networks (image quality, lesion-aware, DR grading); ResNet + Mask-RCNN; ImageNet pretrained
External Validation?: Yes (3 cohorts: CNDCS 92,672 images; NDSP 27,948 images; EyePACS 88,702 images)
Primary Metric Value: Mild NPDR: 0.943 (local), 0.916-0.937 (external); Moderate: 0.955; Severe: 0.960; PDR: 0.972; Referable DR: 0.973
Secondary Metrics: Lesion AUCs: Microaneurysm 0.901, CWS 0.941, Hard exudate 0.954, Hemorrhage 0.967; Image quality AUC 0.934; DME AUC 0.946; Mild NPDR Sens 88.8%, Spec 83.9%
Potential Application: Automated DRSS grading QC; real-time image quality feedback during acquisition; lesion detection for baseline characterization; task shifting for DR screening
Key Findings/Notes: DeepDR is a grading system (not progression prediction). Key innovations: (1) Real-time image quality feedback reduces ungradable images 28.7%→8.2%, improving mild NPDR AUC 0.880→0.933; (2) Lesion-aware sub-network significantly improves primary healthcare workers' grading sensitivity; (3) Multi-task transfer learning architecture. Validated on 3 external cohorts including US (EyePACS). Emphasizes value of detecting mild NPDR for early intervention.
Limitations: Primarily Chinese training cohort; lesion detection only validated locally; uses ICDRDSS not ETDRS/DRSS; cross-sectional grading only - not progression prediction; 2-field imaging may miss peripheral lesions important for progression
